title: Modeling and Simulation of Collective Algorithms on HPC Network Topologies using Structural Simulation Toolkit
problem: Distributed DL training at HPC scale relies on allreduce for gradient synchronization, but evaluating which allreduce and barrier algorithms scale best across different network topologies and message sizes requires simulation since testing on actual supercomputers is impractical.
motivation: As DL training becomes a dominant HPC workload running on the largest supercomputers, optimizing collective communication algorithms across diverse network architectures is critical for improving training performance.
method: The authors extended the Structural Simulation Toolkit (SST) to model allreduce algorithms (Rabenseifner, ring, dissemination) and barrier algorithms (centralized and decentralized). They performed a design space exploration study varying allreduce algorithm choice, barrier algorithm type, network topology (six variants), and message size to measure performance benefits and scaling efficiency.
key_novelty: Extension of SST to enable simulation-based design space exploration of collective algorithms across multiple HPC network topologies, quantifying the performance advantages of locality-preserving algorithm variants.
contributions: Extended Structural Simulation Toolkit to support allreduce (Rabenseifner, ring, dissemination) and barrier algorithm simulation
Conducted design space exploration across three allreduce algorithms, two barrier variants, and six network topologies
Demonstrated performance benefits of locality-preserving allreduce algorithms for HPC communication
Evaluated and compared scaling efficiency of centralized versus decentralized barrier implementations

metrics.speedup: allreduce algorithm performance relative to baseline variants

primary_theme: simulating collective communication algorithms on HPC networks
